rules.objective: Reduce actual routed bounding area and exported QCA cells; both non-increasing, one strictly improved. Distinguish node-box proxy from actual routed area.
rules.routing_execution: One executor-derived complete order after moves; no portfolio fallback.
rules.search_contract: Return a direct gate proposal with routing_order=null; the compiler derives and logs one order using exactly the same rule as the deterministic control. All area/device, exploration, graph identity, clock and physical constraints remain enforced.
rules.proposal_contract: Model synthesizes internal gate coordinates; routing_order=null; executor derives the disclosed deterministic order after placement.
rules.geometry_guidance: Inspect the shared gate-geometry hints as possible starting moves. You may combine or adapt them, or propose new coordinates. Do not repeat a failed geometry merely by swapping the edge list. Use a smaller displacement or a different node subset when routing fails. If moving ports is permitted and they set the outer box, coordinate their relocation with internal gates. Swapping unrelated distant nodes often creates detours; give it a concrete geometric justification.

proposal.rationale: Contract vertical span by shifting the suffix (layers 3–5) down 2 tiles: nodes 13,14,16,18 move from y=25/28→23/26; outputs 5,6 from y=31→29. This reduces height from 12 to 10 while preserving fanin order and avoiding collisions. Vacancy hotspots at (28,23–26) and (22–27,26–29) accommodate moves. Edge detours (e.g., [1,9] with 2 extra steps) suggest local congestion near y=22–25; lowering the middle layer alleviates routing pressure without altering PI/PO envelope width. All moved nodes are internal; port coordinates remain valid within bounds.

Current layout has vertical congestion at y=22–23 (edges [1,9], [9,13], [11,13] detour; multi-source interior sites). Nodes 7 and 8 are adjacent but misaligned with fanin: 7 receives from 2,3; 8 from 0,2. Swapping them places 7 (fanin 2,3) at x=21,y=22 (closer to inputs 2@22,3@26) and 8 at x=26,y=22 (closer to 0@20 via shorter x-path). Moving 13→[28,22] aligns it vertically with 9@28,11@29 (reducing [9,13] and [11,13] detours). Raising 14→[26,24] and 16→[23,25], 18→[28,25] creates a compact vertical stack (y=22→25) for layer 2–4, freeing y=26–29 for outputs and reducing routing crowding near y=23. Vacancy hotspots at (27–29,24–25) and (22–23,25) accommodate moves without collisions. All moved nodes are internal; ports unchanged. This coordinated shift targets the highest-detour edges ([1,9] steps=8, [9,13] steps=1 but constrained by y=22 bottleneck) and reduces Manhattan edge sum by repositioning fanout-heavy nodes toward their sinks.
